close_reason: Ratified to option (A) — keep String inner repr. No code change required; the existing Sha256(String) is the chosen design.
description:
Sha256(String) carries the 64-char hex *wire encoding* as the in-memory representation (crate-jmap-cid-types/src/digest.rs:102), not the canonical 32-byte digest. Idiomatic Rust newtypes over a fixed-size digest store the canonical form ([u8; 32], stack-allocatable, zero allocations, Eq/Hash work over the digest not the hex bytes) and format on demand for Display/Serialize. Compare RustCrypto's Output<Sha256> / GenericArray<u8, U32>.

What goes wrong:
- Heap allocation per Sha256 (the String). [u8; 32] is stack only.
- PartialEq/Hash compare/hash 64 UTF-8 bytes instead of 32 raw bytes. The myoss pass .17 flagged the variable-time issue but the underlying cause is the same — choice of inner representation.
- as_str(&self) -> &str locks in the String backing: switching to [u8; 32] later requires breaking that accessor (no lifetime to hand out from a value derived on the fly). The myoss .13 docs gap and this finding are both downstream of the same representational choice.
- from_bytes pre-allocates a String capacity 64 every call, instead of writing 64 hex chars on demand into the formatter (Display::fmt(&self, f)) with zero allocations.

Idiomatic alternative: Sha256([u8; 32]) with:
- from_hex returning Result<Sha256, Sha256DigestError> — same surface, decodes hex into the byte array.
- from_bytes (or From<[u8; 32]>) trivial — direct field assignment.
- Display computes hex on the fly via fmt::Write into the formatter (no String allocation).
- Serialize via serializer.collect_str(self) — also zero allocation.
- Deserialize via a Visitor that decodes the 64-char input directly into [u8; 32].

This is a pre-v0.1.0 representational choice — fixing later is a public-API break of as_str(), AsRef<str>, into_inner, and From<Sha256> for String. The forward-compat cost of NOT making this choice now is concrete.
title: Sha256 stores derived hex String instead of canonical [u8; 32] — non-idiomatic for a fixed-size digest
